subject: Clarify billing for short sessions + context-rollup behavior
messages:
From: Anita Rao <anita@clearchat.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Liu <tom.liu@clearchat.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Billing for short sessions and context rollups

Hi Ben —

Thanks again for the demo. Two follow-ups from our finance and infra teams:

1) We have a lot of very short chatbot sessions (single-turn prompts) — how does Redwood meter these? Do you round up to a minimum token unit per request or charge exactly by raw tokens?
2) We often stitch multiple short turns into a single user conversation server-side before sending to the model. If we send a concatenated context of prior turns, does Redwood charge on the full request length every time or is there any prefix caching / rollup behavior for repeated context?

Our procurement team is also asking whether pilot discounts can apply if median session length is < 32 tokens. Can you share a short example calculation showing how a 12-token prompt + 20-token response is billed under your model?

Appreciate a quick example so we can include in our SOW.

Best,
Anita Rao\VP Ops, ClearChat
attachments: none
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Anita Rao <anita@clearchat.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 6 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Billing for short sessions and context rollups

Anita — thanks for the great questions. Short answer up front: we charge by actual token usage with a configurable minimum billing quantum on some committed plans, and we offer prefix/KV caching in Dedicated/Private modes which can reduce repeated context charges. Below are practical examples and the options for your pilot.

Example calculation (hosted API, pay-as-you-go):
- Prompt: 12 tokens
- Response: 20 tokens
- Billed: 12 + 20 = 32 tokens (no rounding)

For committed Dedicated seats / reserved capacity customers we optionally apply a per-request minimum of 32 tokens to simplify unit math for high-volume customers; that minimum is not applied to standard hosted accounts unless we agree to it in the contract.

Context rollups and caching: if you append prior turns into the request each time and send it as a full prompt, we bill on the total tokens transmitted. However: in Dedicated and Private deployments we have prefix/KV caching enabled which can avoid re-charging for repeated prefixes in the KV cache for identical context — effectively reducing per-request billable tokens when the runtime can reuse cached KV layers. That behavior depends on exact deployment mode and whether you pin a model variant that supports KV reuse.

Pilot discount: we can offer a 20% pilot usage discount for the first 90 days for accounts where median session length < 32 tokens, applied to billable tokens. If you'd prefer we can instead apply a $X monthly credit; we should confirm with Finance.

I attached a sample usage_report_Q1.csv extract with token breakdowns and a draft SOW (ClearChat_SOW_v2.pdf) with two pilot options (usage discount vs monthly credit). Can we sync Thursday to finalize which path you prefer?

—Ben
Ben Carter\Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Date: Fri, 9 Mar 2028 10:28:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Billing for short sessions and context rollups

Ben / Marissa — quick internal note on margin and operational impact if we accept the 32-token minimum for this pilot:

- Commercial impact: a 32-token per-request minimum for hosted customers materially increases ASP for lots of micro sessions; if ClearChat is small volume it may be fine for the pilot, but we should gate that option to committed monthly commits (e.g., $5k/mo).
- Technical note: prefix KV caching is only guaranteed in Dedicated/Private with the model pinned and matching KV cache semantics. We can include a technical appendix in the SOW that explains caching predicates and when reduced billing applies.
- Legal/procurement: Marissa, please advise on whether Finance needs to approve the 20% pilot discount vs a fixed credit. If we go discount, we need a termination clause that ends the discount after 90 days automatically.

Thoughts? I can draft the short amendment language.

Thanks,
Karthik
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Anita Rao <anita@clearchat.ai>
Cc: Tom Liu <tom.liu@clearchat.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 15:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Billing for short sessions and context rollups

Anita — quick update after internal review and thanks for the patience. We can do the following for ClearChat pilot: 

1) Billing behavior: Hosted pay-as-you-go customers will continue to be billed on exact token usage (no forced minimum). For a 12-token prompt + 20-token response you will be billed for 32 tokens under hosted.

2) Pilot offer for ClearChat (90 days):
   - Option A (Hosted): 20% usage discount on billable tokens for 90 days (automatic expiry). No per-request minimum.
   - Option B (Dedicated short pilot): Reserve a small Dedicated pool for 90 days with KV caching enabled. We will apply a 32-token per-request minimum for the Dedicated pool but provide a $1,200 monthly credit to offset the arithmetic for micro-sessions.

3) Attachments: I re-attached the SOW and a sample usage extract for your finance team. Please confirm which option you prefer and we'll circulate the amendment language + DocuSign link.

Next step: can we lock in a final choice by EOD Friday so Procurement can route the SOW? If yes I will have Marissa draft the amendment and Karthik confirm the technical appendix.

Best,
Ben
